messages.subject: Invisible Lines and Cairo
parts:
Dear All,
I am experiencing something similar to what reported in this thread
http://tinyurl.com/ycqyaro
I am running (X)Ubuntu 9.10 on my machine (amd64 architecture).
I installed a few days ago both ggplot2 (and dependencies) and Cairo
from cran a few days ago.
I refer now to the snippet at the end of the email.
If I use pdf() to save the plot, then the green line becomes invisible
on my machine (but the Delta N_1/N_1 looks OK).
If I resort to CairoPDF(), then lines are OK, but Delta N_1/N_1 gets messy.
Furthermore, it looks like that the text size does not stay the same.
Is anyone experiencing the same problems? This is serious for me right
now since I cannot get a plot involving 4 lines right.
Any help is much appreciated.
Kind Regards

Lorenzo


library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)


link_rem <- seq(0,1,length=100)

n1_strong <- exp(-link_rem)
n1_weak <- exp(-2*link_rem)
n1_onnela <-exp(-3*link_rem)
n1_similarity <-exp(-4*link_rem)

weak <- as.data.frame(cbind(link_rem,n1_weak))

names(weak) <- c("link", "delta_n1")


strong <- as.data.frame(cbind(link_rem,n1_strong))

names(strong) <- c("link", "delta_n1")


onnela <- as.data.frame(cbind(link_rem,n1_onnela))

names(onnela) <- c("link", "delta_n1")

similarity <- as.data.frame(cbind(link_rem,n1_similarity))

names(similarity) <- c("link", "delta_n1")

ml_tmp <- rbind(transform(weak, set="Weak Links"),
transform(strong, set="Strong Links"),transform(onnela,
set="Onnela Links"),transform(similarity, set="Similarity Links"))

lbls <- levels(ml_tmp$set)

gpl <- ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=link, y=delta_n1, colour=set,linetype=set)) +

geom_line(size=1) +
scale_colour_manual("Removal of", breaks=lbls,
labels=lbls,values=c(1,2,3,4)) +
scale_linetype_manual("Removal of", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls,
values=c(1,2,3,5)) +

#extra stuff
xlab(expression(paste("Fraction of Removed Links")))+
ylab(expression(paste(Delta *N[1]/N[1])))+
opts(title = expression(paste("Dublin: July, ",14^th)))+
opts(plot.title = theme_text(size = 18))+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 18))+
opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 14, vjust=0.8))+
opts(legend.title = theme_text(size = 18,hjust=0))+
opts(legend.position = c(0.4, 0.3),
legend.background=theme_rect(fill='white'))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray", hjust=1))


fn <- paste("test_link_removal.pdf")

CairoPDF(fn)
#pdf(fn)
print(gpl)
dev.off()

messages.subject: Re: Invisible Lines and Cairo
parts:
Hi,

As far as I can see it's still the same bug, hopefully it'll be fixed
in the next release of R.

It is now possible to set lineend to another value than "butt", but
only for geom_path (not for geom_line for some reason?),

geom_path(size=1, lineend="round")

With this amendment the line reappears in the pdf output,
unfortunately the legend grob does not consider this parameter so it
doesn't help you here.

Best,

baptiste

messages.author: d9db8f5076586bc3
messages.subject: Changing the font size of text elements
parts:
Dear all,

I am finding out I often need to change the font size of ggplot plots
(because the text elements do not get resized automatically as the
rest of the plot).

I have been struggling with the lazy evaluation mechanism, that does
not let me get it right. I am sure I am missing something obvious,
but I cannot find out what it is.
My code is below.
What happens now is that all text elements get the properties of the
last element in my list, I believe because of the lazy evaluation. I
would appreciate any hints.
Best,
Pedro

====================================
Fun1 <- function(Plot, PropChange = 1)
{
###Purpose
###Changes the font size used in the different elements of a ggplot object
###by a fixed proportion
###########################################################################
activeOptions <- Plot$options
textOptions <- c("axis.title.x", "axis.title.y", "axis.text.x"
, "axis.text.y", "legend.text", "legend.title"
, "strip.text.x", "strip.text.y")
nOptions <- length(textOptions)
R <- vector(mode="list", length = nOptions)
family <- vector(mode = "character", length = nOptions)
face <- vector(mode = "character", length = nOptions)
colour <- vector(mode = "character", length = nOptions)
size = vector(mode = "numeric", length = nOptions)
hjust = vector(mode = "numeric", length = nOptions)
vjust = vector(mode = "numeric", length = nOptions)
angle = vector(mode = "numeric", length = nOptions)
lineheight = vector(mode = "numeric", length = nOptions)


names(R) <- textOptions
for(i in 1:nOptions){
objName <- textOptions[i]
if(objName %in% names(activeOptions)){
txt1 <- Plot$options[[objName]]("a")
}else{
txt1 <- theme_get()[[objName]]("a")
}
Options <- txt1$gp
family[i] <- Options[["fontfamily"]]
face[i] = Options[["fontface"]]
colour[i] = Options[["col"]]
size[i] = Options[["fontsize"]]* PropChange
hjust[i] = txt1$hjust
vjust[i] = txt1$vjust
angle[i] = txt1$rot
lineheight[i] = Options[["lineheight"]]
R[[i]] <- theme_text(family = family[i]
, face = face[i]
, colour = colour[i]
, size = size[i]
, hjust = hjust[i]
, vjust = vjust[i]
, angle = angle[i]
, lineheight = lineheight[i])
}
R <- Plot + structure(R, class ="options")
return(R)
}

Hi Baptiste,
Thanks a lot for the help.
I tried, and it worked, but I wanted something that would actually
create a call to theme_text, and based on your suggestion I wrote the
one below. Maybe someone can make use of some of the ideas...

Thanks again,
Pedro
===================================================
f.ggPlotChangeFontSize <- function(Plot, PropChange = 1)

{
###Purpose
###Changes the font size used in the different elements of a ggplot object
###by a fixed proportion
###########################################################################
activeOptions <- Plot$options
textOptions <- c("axis.title.x", "axis.title.y", "axis.text.x"
, "axis.text.y", "legend.text", "legend.title"
, "strip.text.x", "strip.text.y")
nOptions <- length(textOptions)
R <- vector(mode="list", length = nOptions)
names(R) <- textOptions

for(i in 1:nOptions){
objName <- textOptions[i]
if(objName %in% names(activeOptions)){
txt1 <- Plot$options[[objName]]("a")
}else{
txt1 <- theme_get()[[objName]]("a")
}
Options <- txt1$gp

FUN1 <- function(family, face, colour, size, hjust, vjust, angle,
lineheight){theme_text(family = family
, face = face
, colour = colour
, size = size
, hjust = hjust
, vjust = vjust
, angle = angle
, lineheight = lineheight)}
R[[i]] <- do.call(FUN1, list(family = Options[["fontfamily"]]
, face = Options[["fontface"]]
, colour = Options[["col"]]
, size = Options[["fontsize"]]* PropChange
, hjust = txt1$hjust
, vjust = txt1$vjust
, angle = txt1$rot
, lineheight = Options[["lineheight"]]))

}
R <- Plot + structure(R, class ="options")
return(R)
}
